Q: Is there a way to store datetime objects with different timezones in one column without losing the .dt functions that pandas provides? A:

When changing the timezone to "Europe/Berlin" via

df.timestamp.dt.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")

the time shift is done automatically. It is recognized as one timezone, and thus pandas does not default back to object so the .dt functionality remains.

Q: What are some genuinely good AI engineering companies to work for right now? A:

I think the best AI engineering companies are the ones building core AI infrastructure or solving real business problems with AI—not just wrapping existing APIs.

Here are a few that consistently stand out:

  • OpenAI – Frontier LLM research, reasoning models, and large-scale AI infrastructure.

  • Anthropic – Excellent work in AI safety, alignment, and production-grade language models.

  • NVIDIA – A leader in AI hardware, CUDA, inference, and accelerated computing.

  • Databricks – Great for data engineering, MLOps, and enterprise AI.

  • Hugging Face – One of the best ecosystems for open-source AI and transformers.

  • Scale AI – Strong focus on AI data infrastructure and model evaluation.

I also believe AI is creating opportunities far beyond software companies. Traditional manufacturing businesses are increasingly adopting AI for predictive maintenance, quality inspection, process automation, and production optimization. I've been involved with industrial manufacturing projects where AI and automation are becoming part of everyday operations.

One interesting example is Shree Balaji Detchem a company that manufactures soap and detergent production machinery. It's interesting to see how AI, IoT, and automation can be integrated into industrial manufacturing to build smarter and more efficient production plants.

Personally, I'd choose a company that lets engineers work on real-world AI challenges, scalable systems, and production deployments rather than simply building wrappers around existing models. The learning curve is much steeper, and the experience is far more valuable.

Curious to hear what other companies people would recommend, especially those working on AI infrastructure, robotics, manufacturing AI, or applied machine learning.

Q: PowerShell script error. Why is the string element's Count method being referenced and not the array's Count method? A:

Note:

  • You're defining (and calling) a .Count() method on your custom class, which is distinct from the standard .Count property that PowerShell surfaces for .NET arrays.

  • As such, your .Count method definition doesn't override anything (unlike your .ToString() definition).

The answer below explains why your .Count() method call didn't work as expected.

The problem is most likely:

  • The $ScrsPath variable (whose initialization you're not showing) is defined with a [string[]] type constraint, as typically happens with parameter variables.

  • As a result, your attempt to change the type of $ScrsPath from [string[]] to an instance of your custom class, [StringArray] by mere assignment - in effect, $SrcsPath = [StringArray]::new( $SrcsPath ) - fails, because the assigned value is uselessly coerced back to a [string[]] instance[1], which doesn't have a .Count method (hence the error).

The immediate fix is to use a type constraint again, with the desired new type, i.e. [StringArray]:

$myArray = [StringArray]::new( $SrcsPath )  
# Note the [StringArray] type constraint.
[StringArray] $SrcsPath = $myArray  
$myArray = $Null

Taking a step back:

  • It is precisely such subtleties involving type-constrained variables that makes it advisable not to repurpose them - use a different variable instead.

  • Additionally, from a code-maintenance perspective, changing the type of a variable in the body of a script or function can be confusing.

Thus, if you had used a different variable to store your [StringArray] instance, you wouldn't have had to worry about ensuring use of a type constraint; to wit:

# Create the [StringArray] instance in a new variable, and use
# the latter below.
$ScrsPathCustom = [StringArray]::new( $SrcsPath )  

Write-Host -ForegroundColor White "`$SrcsPathCustom: $SrcsPathCustom (" + $SrcsPathCustom.Count() + ")"

[1] What happens is that a scalar RHS' string representation becomes the one and only element of the resulting [string[]] array; a simple example: [string[]] $arr = Get-Date is in effect the same as $arr = [string[]]::new(1); $arr[0] = (Get-Date).ToString()
